title: What I Learned From a Year of Interviewing a Thai Sex Worker
author: Toh Oon Hoe
text:
Illuminated signs on “Walking Street” in Pattaya, Thailand, a focus of the city’s sex industry.
Credit: Wikimedia Commons/FritzDaCat
When I started interviewing a Thai sex worker named Ying for my recent book, I was initially looking for something far different from what I eventually wrote. I wanted sleaze: something raw and stimulating. I had wanted to write about a harlot, someone immoral, for whom money took precedence over all. I had expected to write about their greed, their lack of morals and the hypocrisy that arose from an industry surrounding a deeply religious society.My assumptions were both critical and ignorant. In every way, I had already decided on the book I was going to write without attempting to understand the mechanics or psychology behind them. What I have since learned is about choices, and how few meaningful ones there were for someone caught between family obligation, economic status, and religion. What I learned was about the life of a tortured soul, fighting to make the best of what she had.[...]
